releases.title: collectZ v3.27.3
releases.summary: Makes the provider-connection-scoped external identity registry authoritative for adopted sync paths while preserving existing provider fields as compatibility projections. The release establishes stable canonical UUIDs, lifecycle-safe provider identities, conflict-safe merge and revert behavior, canonical field precedence, and explicit cutover diagnostics without removing legacy fields.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added immutable canonical object UUIDs, multi-instance Provider Connections, scoped external identities, append-only lifecycle evidence, and explicit workspace integration bindings.
Added authorized transaction composition for identity attach, resolve, deactivate, reassign, merge, revert, compatibility projection, and canonical field decisions.
Added plan-first, fail-closed legacy identity backfill that attaches only unambiguous evidence and reports duplicate, conflicting, or unbound rows without guessing.

Added Canonical Field Controls so provider refreshes preserve uncontrolled existing, manual, reviewed, locked, and differently sourced values unless an explicit reviewed refresh policy permits replacement.
Adopted authoritative reconciliation in Metron, CWA/Calibre OPDS, and Plex imports. Plex prefers GUID identity and falls back to its section/item key when a GUID is absent.

Added bounded compatibility telemetry and deterministic cutover diagnostics. A provider requires at least seven continuous observation days, two successful syncs, no legacy activity or projection conflicts, repeat-alignment evidence, and a clean legacy inventory before a separate cutover proposal.
Updated `fast-xml-parser` to `5.12.0` after the release audit identified the stop-node CPU-consumption advisory affecting `5.11.2`; the rebuilt backend now reports zero dependency vulnerabilities.
Preserved compatibility fields and existing provider behavior; BookOrbit remains scoped to `3.27.4`, and Kavita authoritative adoption remains scoped to `3.27.5`.

releases.title: collectZ v3.27.2
releases.summary: Updates the application runtime, provider HTTP transport, rate limiting, mail transport, object-storage client, and frontend build tooling before provider-identity and BookOrbit implementation resumes.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Updated Express from `5.2.1` to `5.3.0` and express-rate-limit from `8.7.1` to `8.7.2`.
Updated backend Axios from `1.20.0` to `1.21.0` before BookOrbit begins using the shared provider HTTP seam.
Updated Nodemailer from `10.2.1` to `10.3.1` and AWS SDK S3 from `3.1156.0` to `3.1162.0`.
Updated frontend esbuild from `0.28.1` to `0.28.2` without changing Vite, Vitest, React, Tailwind, or ZXing.
Kept the existing security overrides until the installed graph proves they are no longer required.

releases.title: collectZ v3.27.1
releases.summary: Canonical media objects now have immutable collectZ UUIDs, while provider identifiers live in a separate, workspace-safe registry scoped to stable provider connections.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Add a collectZ-generated `media.public_id` UUID without replacing the existing numeric primary key or internal foreign keys.
Add multi-instance `provider_connections` with stable UUID identity, explicit active/disabled/archived lifecycle, validated provider settings, and separately stored encrypted credential payloads.

Add provider-connection-scoped external media identities with raw and normalized values, concrete canonical media targets, first/last-seen timestamps, safe source URLs, active/deactivated history, and append-only lifecycle events.
Enforce active identity uniqueness by workspace, provider connection, identity kind, and normalized external id, allowing two installations of the same provider to use the same local id safely.
Add database-enforced workspace consistency between media and libraries and between external identities, provider connections, and media targets.
Protect every new workspace-owned identity table with RLS from its first migration and route identity operations through authorized transactions.
Add adapter-owned settings, credential, and external-id normalization contracts plus the `resolve`, `attach`, `listForMedia`, `deactivate`, and transactional `reassign` identity interface.
Record the identity decision and rejected alternatives in `docs/adr/0001-canonical-object-and-provider-identity.md`.

releases.title: collectZ v3.27.0
releases.summary: Database workflows can now use one tested transaction executor for connection acquisition, isolation selection, commit, rollback, failed-rollback disposal, bounded retry, and sanitized diagnostics.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Add `executeTransaction(pool, work, options)` as the common database transaction interface.
Limit isolation selection to PostgreSQL `READ COMMITTED`, `REPEATABLE READ`, and `SERIALIZABLE` modes.
Keep retry disabled by default and permit at most two explicitly requested retries, only for serialization failures and deadlocks.
Discard connections after failed `BEGIN` or failed rollback so uncertain transaction state cannot return to the pool.
Emit optional timing/outcome diagnostics without SQL, parameters, error messages, or credentials; diagnostic sink failures cannot alter transaction results.
Rebuild authorized saved-view scoped transactions on the executor without moving authorization into the executor.
Adopt the interface for feature-flag default persistence as the first low-risk database-only workflow.
Add interface tests for success, work/query/commit failure, rollback failure, disposal, isolation, bounded retries, and diagnostic sanitization.

releases.title: collectZ v3.26.0
releases.summary: Saved library views now use database-enforced workspace, library, and owner isolation in addition to existing application authorization.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Bind saved-view CRUD to one authorized transaction and commit before returning an HTTP success.

A narrowly privileged, separately authenticated scope broker grants access only to a specific runtime role, backend PID, full transaction ID, actor, workspace, and optional library. Grants expire after five minutes and are removed after work finishes.
Enable SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies on saved views; reject ownership changes and guard referential-action deletes that bypass RLS.
Deny unscoped SQL and spoofed settings; retain existing application permission checks.
Patch the existing `follow-redirects` overrides to `1.16.2` in both applications to clear the newly reported redirect credential-leak advisory without updating Axios.
Certify runtime isolation, upgrade/backfill, rollback, concurrent connections, expiry, and snapshot restore in the existing PostgreSQL service locally and in hosted migration-check.

releases.title: collectZ v3.25.4
releases.summary: Updates compatible backend and frontend dependencies represented by ten Dependabot PRs, consolidating the changes into one tested release. Keeps the barcode package pair and GitHub Actions major updates under separate compatibility review.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Backend: update `@aws-sdk/client-s3`, `axios`, `fast-xml-parser`, `helmet`, and `pg` within their existing major-version ranges.
Frontend: update React, React DOM, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, Tailwind CSS, and its Vite plugin within their existing major-version ranges.
Keep `@zxing/browser` and `@zxing/library` together for a focused compatibility check; `@zxing/browser@0.2.1` requires `@zxing/library@^0.23.0`.
Keep GitHub Actions major upgrades under separate workflow compatibility review.
Synchronize application metadata and Help > Releases to `3.25.4`.

releases.title: collectZ v3.25.3
releases.summary: Updates vulnerable backend runtime dependencies and frontend test tooling to patched compatible releases following fresh full dependency audits.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Update affected backend packages and transitive dependencies: `body-parser@2.4.0`, `multer@2.5.0`, `nodemailer@10.2.1`, `ip-address@10.7.4`, and `zod@4.6.7`.
Update frontend `vitest` and `@vitest/mocker` to `4.1.12`.
Preserve the established Node `24.22.1` baseline and avoid unrelated major-version changes; `express@5.2.1` was already present before this release.
Synchronize application metadata and Help > Releases to `3.25.3`.

releases.title: collectZ v3.25.2
releases.summary: Remediates reported vulnerabilities in CollectZ's development and build tooling. Vite and its source-map dependency are upgraded to fixed releases, and the backend development command now uses Node's built-in watch mode instead of Nodemon and its affected watcher tree.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Upgrade frontend Vite from affected `8.0.16` to `8.3.5` and lock `source-map-js` to `1.2.2`, addressing the reported Vite/launch-editor and source-map-js advisories.

Replace `nodemon server.js` with `node --watch server.js` and remove Nodemon from backend development dependencies. This removes the backend watcher chain that included vulnerable `braces` and `brace-expansion` packages.
Keep backend and frontend production dependencies on the previously patched `follow-redirects@1.16.1`.
Synchronize app metadata and Help > Releases to `3.25.2`.

releases.title: collectZ v3.25.1
releases.summary: Moves CollectZ's Node 24 runtime, build, CI, and operational helper environments to Node `24.22.1`, the security-fixed Node 24 maintenance-LTS release. The previous canonical backend container was running Node `24.21.0`, which predates the October 21 security release.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Pin backend and frontend build images, syslog and sizing helper images, and the local dependency-audit image to `node:24.22.1-alpine`.
Pin active Node-based GitHub Actions workflows to Node `24.22.1` and add `.nvmrc` for maintainers.
Raise the declared minimum backend engine to `>=24.22.1 <25` and add source-contract coverage for all maintained runtime and CI selectors.
Update the backend and frontend `follow-redirects` override from `1.16.0` to `1.16.1` to resolve two newly reported high-severity advisories found during release preflight.
Document that `npm audit` covers package dependencies, not the Node runtime and its bundled OpenSSL, c-ares, CA certificates, and Undici components.

releases.title: collectZ v3.25.0
releases.summary: Adds a native Apple TV companion for CollectZ with browser-approved sign-in, read-only collection browsing, and the existing CollectZ visual identity. The SwiftUI client is maintained in the sibling `collectZ-tvos` repository.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: TV pairing and browsing work in both deployment modes, including installations with Cairn. Every read still requires current library/workspace membership; archived workspaces are excluded.
Native screens use only the CollectZ name. Debug simulator builds recognize bare localhost and private IPv4 LAN addresses as HTTP; public connections and Release builds still require HTTPS.
Browser `/activate` approval uses short-lived device codes, existing cookie authentication, and CSRF protection. Device credentials/codes are hashed; polling is limited and redemption is atomic.
Dedicated TV permissions reuse mobile access/refresh sessions. Existing scanner permissions are unchanged. TV sessions cannot edit data, trigger imports, or use capture APIs.
Explicit library selection checks current membership on every read, including administrator accounts, without changing the web application's active library.
TV responses expose safe metadata and authorized artwork paths rather than raw integration payloads or source URLs. Collection joins check linked media ownership.
Native tvOS 18+ screens use CollectZ's colors, logo, bundled fonts, cards, and badges, with remote focus, accessible labels, stale states, and Keychain credentials.
Updated compatible axios and proxy-addr lockfile resolutions to remove production dependency advisories identified during release validation.
